
```{r}
# Arranging the Order - Slide 11-17
## Task 1
penguins |> arrange(body_mass) |> relocate(body_mass, .after = island) |> head()

## Task 2
penguins |> arrange(desc(flipper_len)) |> relocate(flipper_len, .after = island) |> head()

## Task 3
penguins |> group_by(species) |> arrange(bill_len) |> relocate(bill_len, .after = island)
### alt. solution (slide 12)
penguins |> arrange(species, desc(bill_len))

## Task 4
penguins |> relocate(bill_dep, bill_len, flipper_len, body_mass, .after =species)

## Task 5
penguins |> relocate(year, .after = sex)

## Challenge
penguins |> arrange(desc(body_mass)) |> relocate(body_mass, bill_dep, bill_len, flipper_len, .before = species)
```


```{r}
# Keeping or Removing Data
## Task No. 1 - Filter Adelie penguins

penguins |> filter(species == "Adelie") |> count()

## Task No. 2 - Which Island has most penguins
penguins |> count(island)

## Task No. 3 - Display all Gentoo Penguins which have a body mass greater than 5.000 g
penguins |> filter(species == "Gentoo" & body_mass > 5000) |> relocate(body_mass, .after = island)

## Task No. 4 - For how many penguins do we have sex data
penguins |> filter(sex > 0) |> count()

## Task No. 5 - I define a small penguin as weighing less than 3500g and having a bill shorter than 35mm. How many penguins meet this criteria?
penguins |> filter(body_mass < 3500 & bill_len < 35) |> count()
```


```{r}
#Usage of Select
##Task No. 1 - Use select() and starts_with() to keep all columns that measure a physical feature of the penguins (bill_len, bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass).

penguins |> select(starts_with("b") | starts_with("f")) |> head()
```


```{r}
# Distinct Function
## Task No. 1 - For each penguin species, identify which islands they are found on.

penguins |> distinct(species, island)

## Task No. 2 - Filter for penguins with a body mass greater than 4000g, then find the distinct species-sex combinations (e.g., among ‘big’ penguins, are there both males and females from all species, or are only some species/sexes present).

penguins |> filter(body_mass > 4000) |> distinct(species, sex) |> head()

## Task No. 3 - Filter for Gentoo penguins from the Biscoe island. How many distinct years were they sampled in?

penguins |> filter(species == "Gentoo" & island == "Biscoe") |> distinct(year) |> head()
```


```{r}
# Working with mutate

## Task No. 1 - Create a new variable called body_mass_kg.

penguins |> 
  mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass / 1000) |>  
  select(contains("body")) |> 
  head()

## Task No. 2 - Create a new variable flipper_to_mass_ratio, and sort it in decreasing order. - This is called a derived variable and is extremely useful.

penguins |> 
  mutate(flipper_to_mass_ratio = flipper_len / body_mass) |> 
  arrange(desc(flipper_to_mass_ratio)) |> 
  select(contains("f") | contains("body")) |> 
  relocate(flipper_to_mass_ratio, .after = body_mass)
  head()

## Task No. 3 - Create a new variable called heavy indicating whether body_mass is greater than 4.5kg.
penguins |> 
  mutate(heavy = body_mass > 4500) |> 
  select(contains("species") | contains("island") | contains("heavy"))
  head()
```
